subject: PO header requirements, invoice pulse and net-term carveout
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarcare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO header requirements, invoice pulse and net-term carveout

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time on Thursday. Per follow-up from procurement, we want to confirm the exact PO and invoicing expectations so Finance can scope the billing workflow before we finalize the SOW. Quick summary of what we need from you:

- PO format: is the PO number required in the invoice header (top-level) or is it acceptable as an invoice line-level reference?
- Invoice cadence: your team mentioned a weekly pulse for partial deliveries vs a consolidated monthly statement — can you confirm which is mandatory for payment processing?
- Net terms: current ask on our side is Net60. If that conflicts with StellarCare policy, what is the earliest term you can sign up to?

I attached the draft SOW and our invoice template (redwood-invoice-template.xlsx) to show how we populate PO and cost-center fields.

If PO header is required and weekly stubs are mandatory, we can support both but it will affect our operational cadence (we'd want to reconcile to a consolidated monthly statement for crediting). Is your AP team ok with receiving weekly invoice stubs plus one monthly statement?

Next steps: if you can share a sample PO or the procurement checklist, we’ll map fields and flag any gaps. Looping in Karthik for procurement logistics.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-invoice-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_Redwood-v2.docx (doc)

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarcare.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarcare.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:48:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: PO header requirements, invoice pulse and net-term carveout

Aditya —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few points from procurement / AP after reviewing your template:

1) PO placement: StellarCare requires PO number in the invoice header (top of invoice). We cannot process invoices that only reference a PO in a line-item field.
2) Invoice cadence: for services that are recognized weekly (time / usage), our AP needs weekly invoice stubs for routing and matching. We then accept a consolidated monthly statement for payment netting, but the weekly stubs must be sent and match the PO and GL cost center.
3) Net terms: our standard is Net45 for vendors without approved prepay. Net60 is outside policy and will require VP Finance approval. We can consider Net60 as an exception if we receive a 3% early-pay discount window (Net30 at 3% / Net60 otherwise) OR a partial prepayment on signature.
4) Metadata requirements: every invoice must include PO ID, internal cost center code, and a reference to the purchase reason (SKU or SOW paragraph ID).

I attached a sanitized sample PO and our procurement checklist. If you can accept PO in header + weekly stubs + consolidated monthly statement, we can route this for a Net60 exception with the early-pay discount as an alternative. Otherwise Net45 is the default.

-Maya
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager
StellarCare Health
Attachments: PO_StellarCare_20270601.pdf (pdf), procurement-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarcare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO header requirements, invoice pulse and net-term carveout

Maya —

Thanks for the clarity and for the sample PO. We can comply with the PO-in-header requirement and produce weekly invoice stubs that match the PO and cost center. Operationally, our preferred reconciliation is to deliver the weekly stubs (for matching) and a consolidated monthly statement that nets those stubs into a single payable amount — this keeps collections predictable for both parties.

On the net-term point: two proposals from our side so we can move this forward without VP-level cycle time:

Option A (preferred): Net60 with a 1.25% early-pay discount if paid by Net30. This reduces your short-term cash burden while giving StellarCare an incentive to pay earlier when helpful.

Option B: Start with Net45 for the first 3 months, then move to Net60 after a positive payment track record (no disputes, on-time matching of weekly stubs).

We are also open to a small holdback (e.g., 5% of each monthly consolidated invoice) released after the first quarter as an assurance mechanism if that is helpful for AP.

Please let us know which option is preferable and we’ll draft an amendment and a DocuSign link. Attaching: revised invoice template with PO header field flagged.

Best,
Aditya
Attachments: redwood-invoice-template.xlsx (updated)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarcare.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO header requirements, invoice pulse and net-term carveout

Hi team —

Looping in to lock this down. After speaking briefly with StellarCare’s AP, they are willing to accept Option B: start Net45 for the first quarter, then move to Net60 provided weekly stubs and the consolidated monthly statement reconcile cleanly and there are no invoice disputes. They also agreed to include the PO number in the invoice header and require the cost-center mapping per the attached sample.

Action items:
- Aditya: I will draft a short billing amendment (1-paragraph) capturing the initial Net45 term, weekly stub requirement, consolidated monthly statement, and a 3-month review to transition to Net60. I will include a 5% holdback clause to be released after Q1 if reconciliation is clean.
- Karthik: please prepare the invoice metadata mapping (PO header, cost center -> GL code mapping) and a short note for StellarCare AP so they can auto-accept the stub format.
- Maya: once we send the amendment I will share a DocuSign link for signature.

I attached the proposed amendment text and a link to the HubSpot deal where I captured the payment terms.

Thanks — will follow up with DocuSign this afternoon.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: amendment-billing-term-draft.docx (doc), https://app.hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-8942
